Hi Anya / MedCore procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great alignment on the pilot scope. To keep momentum we put together a short decision path and a commitment matrix (attached) that lays out the minimal sequencing we need from both sides to close in the next 10 business days. Quick summary below and a couple of asks: please confirm ownership and target dates by end of day Wednesday.

High-level MAP (milestones & owners)
- Legal redline review (MedCore legal) — target: 3 business days from receipt of redline
- Redwood responds to redlines (Karthik) — 2 business days after receiving MedCore redline
- DPA execution or signed addendum — targeted to sign concurrently with MSA
- Order form & pricing sign-off (Procurement + Revenue ops) — final sign and execute after MSA/DPA agreed
- SOC2 / security evidence delivery — Redwood to provide current SOC2 report and subprocessor list before signature

Primary asks for you:
1) Confirm whether MedCore prefers an integrated DPA inside the MSA or a separate DPA addendum.
2) Share the name and email of the legal reviewer and an expected turnaround (3 business days would be ideal).
3) Any procurement template clauses (PO number, payment terms) we should preload into the order form.

Attachments: rdw_map_v2.xlsx (MAP + commitment matrix), draft_order_form_v0.3.pdf

If those dates work, we can route a redline-ready MSA to your counsel today and aim to have signatures before the end of next week.

Thanks Vanessa — looks helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement/legal:

1) MedCore prefers the DPA as a separate, signed addendum to the MSA. We have a standard clause set for data residency and subprocessors that we need applied.
2) Our lead counsel will be Anya Malik (anya.malik@medcore.com). Turnaround: target 3 business days but could slip to 5 if we need to loop in compliance for HCLS items.
3) Procurement: Net 45 payment terms, PO required before invoice. If Redwood can accept a 45-day term we can include PO details on the order form.

On security: please send SOC2 report and the current subprocessor list — procurement will confirm if that satisfies internal requirements before signature.

We have two immediate blockers that could affect timeline: indemnity cap language and any clauses that imply data localization beyond what we already discussed. If Redwood can propose language on indemnity cap and an explicit subprocessors appendix, that will speed review.

Anya

Vanessa / team — I parsed MedCore's ask and sketched a recommended sequencing and a short list of legal items that need to be resolved before signature. High-level summary below; attaching an initial redline to accelerate.

Top legal items (impact / suggested approach)
- Indemnity & cap: MedCore has asked to tighten indemnity exposure. Suggest: propose a mutual cap tied to 12 months of fees for the pilot/order form; flag any carve-outs for IP infringement.
- Data residency / localization: confirm exact regulatory requirement. If MedCore requires EU-only processing for certain datasets, we'll provide a scoped data-processing appendix.
- Subprocessors: provide current subprocessor list and include a 30-day notification + objection window in the DPA.
- Audit rights / SOC2: we will deliver SOC2 report; if MedCore requests an on-site audit, we need to slot scheduling (this typically adds 2–3 weeks).
- Liability language and consequential damages: push for mutual limitations where possible; be prepared to carve out willful misconduct.

Recommended sequencing to preserve close velocity
1) Exchange redlines on MSA (MedCore -> Redwood) — target 3 business days
2) Redwood responds with tracked changes + proposed cap language (Karthik) — 2 business days
3) Execute DPA as a separate addendum simultaneous with MSA signature (we can sign DPA at the same time as MSA to avoid sequential delay)
4) Order form finalized and signed (Revenue ops) — this can be executed concurrently with MSA/DPA once payment terms and PO flow are agreed

If MedCore insists on an independent legal window for the DPA, we can still parallelize: ask procurement to approve the order form subject to DPA signature. That preserves go-live timing while legal finishes the DPA.

I've attached: redline_msa_karthik.docx (initial comments focused on indemnity, liability, and data processing).

I'll be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow morning to walk counsel through the redline if that helps.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
